name: Crosswater
label: Crosswater
about_prose: Crosswater sits on 600 acres of woodland and preserved wetland adjacent to Sunriver and Caldera Springs in Deschutes County, about 15 miles south of Bend. The Deschutes and Little Deschutes Rivers run through the property, crossing the golf course as many as seven times in a round depending on which tees you play. The community is private and gated, developed decades after the surrounding area. Sunriver itself dates to 1968, built on the grounds of Camp Abbot, a World War II Army training site that closed in 1944.

The golf course opened in 1995, designed by Robert E. Cupp in a heathland style. It played 7,683 yards from the championship tees, the longest course in the country at the time it opened. Bent grass covers the fairways and greens, with five tee placements per hole and a course rating of 76.5 against a slope of 145. Golf Digest named it Best New Resort Course of 1995, ranked it as high as 28th nationally in 2005-06, and placed it 69th on America's 100 Greatest Public Courses for 2025-26, along with 11th best in Oregon. Golfweek ranks it 17th among the country's best residential golf courses. The course has hosted the JELD-WEN Tradition, a PGA Tour Champions major, for four years running from 2007 through 2010, plus the PGA Professional National Championship and NCAA Division I championships.

Ownership at Crosswater comes in three forms. Ninety-four estate lots sit around the course, two of them consolidated so 92 are buildable. Seven Canoe Camp homes and 23 Osprey Pointe condominiums round out the count. Some Osprey Pointe units are also offered through Sunriver Resort's vacation rental program, so not every neighbor there is a full-time owner. Everything is governed through the Crosswater Club, which runs The Grille restaurant and the pro shop, and gives members access to Sage Springs Spa and Fitness. Three miles of walking and biking trails run through the community's wetlands and common area.

The course itself is not open to the public. It is reserved for Crosswater Club members and Sunriver Resort guests, so buying a lot or a home here means buying into club membership, not just a golf-course address. Membership also opens access to the wider Sunriver network, including the SHARC aquatic center and additional golf, under the terms of your ownership and membership agreement. Golf access at Crosswater runs through the club, not through the property title alone.

Sunriver Village, with its grocery store and shops, is about 5 minutes away. Bend, and the fuller range of retail, dining, and services that comes with it, is about 20 minutes north. Kids in the area attend Three Rivers School, a K-8 school run by Bend-La Pine Schools with roughly 420 students, the only school inside Sunriver. There is no high school in Sunriver itself. Families send teenagers on to Caldera High School in Bend or La Pine High School in La Pine, a real commute worth weighing before you buy.

The broader Sunriver area was named a Dark Sky Friendly Development of Distinction by DarkSky International in August 2020, the first such designation in Oregon. The recognition reflects a sustained, area-wide effort to control outdoor lighting, and it shows on a clear night. Combined with the wetlands and the two rivers, the tree cover across the 600 acres gives Crosswater the feel of a private reserve as much as a golf community.
